Class MediaVaultController

java.lang.Object
MediaVaultController
public class MediaVaultController extends Object
Coordinates every interaction between the MediaVault model and its JavaFX view. The controller is the only class that holds both sides at once: it pulls raw text out of the view, validates it, drives the model, then pushes finished Strings back to the view for display.

The view is never given a MediaEntry, a Library, a UserProfile, or a MediaStatus. Anything the view shows has already been converted to a String here, which keeps the presentation layer completely free of model types. Equally, the controller never touches a JavaFX node; page switching is asked for through named view methods such as mainPage and swapFront.

Each account owns its own save file, named after the user. Logging in reads that file into the working library; signing up creates it.

  • Constructor Details

    • MediaVaultController

      public MediaVaultController(Library library, MediaVaultView view, FileManager fileManager)
      Constructs a controller bound to the given model, view, and file manager.

      Precondition: library, view, and fileManager are not null
      Postcondition: the controller holds all three collaborators, with no user logged in and no event handlers registered yet

      Parameters:
      library - the Library holding all media entries
      view - the MediaVaultView the user interacts with
      fileManager - the FileManager used to save and load the library

  • Method Details

    • initController

      public void initController()
      Registers every event handler with the view and shows the login page, so the program opens asking who is using it.

      Postcondition: all view controls are wired to their handlers and the login page is showing

    • handleLogin

      public void handleLogin()
      Signs an existing user in. The username must not be blank and must have a save file already, which is what distinguishes an existing account from a new one. On success the user's saved entries are read into the working library and the main page is shown.

      Postcondition: on success a profile is active, the library holds that user's saved entries, and the main page is showing; otherwise a message is placed on the login page and nothing else changes

    • handleSignup

      public void handleSignup()
      Creates a new account. The username must not be blank and must not already have a save file. On success an empty save file is written so that the account exists on disk, and the main page is shown.

      Postcondition: on success a new empty library and save file exist for the user and the main page is showing; otherwise a message is placed on the sign-up page and nothing else changes

    • handleSwapFront

      public void handleSwapFront()
      Switches the front page between login and sign-up. The decision of which page is currently showing belongs to the view, so this simply asks it to swap.

      Postcondition: the login and sign-up pages have swapped

    • handleAddEntry

      public void handleAddEntry()
      Reads the entry fields from the view, validates them, and adds a new entry of the selected media type to the library. Duplicate titles, blank required fields, and non-numeric values in numeric fields are all rejected with a message rather than allowed through.

      Postcondition: a new entry is added only when every field is valid; the view is refreshed and told the outcome either way

    • handleRemoveEntry

      public void handleRemoveEntry()
      Removes the entry currently selected in the view from the library.

      Postcondition: the selected entry is removed when one is selected and found; the view is refreshed and told the outcome

    • handleUpdateStatus

      public void handleUpdateStatus()
      Applies the status currently chosen in the view to the entry currently selected in the view.

      Postcondition: the selected entry's status is updated when both a valid entry and a valid status are chosen

    • handleRateAndReview

      public void handleRateAndReview()
      Attaches a rating and review to the entry currently selected in the view. The completion rule is checked here before prompting the model, and the model enforces it again as a safety net.

      Postcondition: the rating and review are stored only when the entry is COMPLETED and the rating is within the valid range

    • handleFilter

      public void handleFilter()
      Filters the displayed list by the media type and status currently chosen in the view. Either selector may be left on its "None" option, in which case that dimension is not narrowed.

      Postcondition: the view shows only entries matching the chosen filters; the library itself is unchanged

    • handleSearch

      public void handleSearch()
      Searches the library for entries whose title or genre contains the keyword currently typed in the view. An empty keyword restores the full list rather than matching nothing.

      Postcondition: the view shows the matching entries; the library itself is unchanged

    • handleSave

      public void handleSave()
      Writes the current library to the logged-in user's save file and then logs them out, returning the interface to the login page. Any input or output failure is reported to the user instead of escaping.

      Postcondition: on success the save file reflects the library and no user is logged in; on failure the user stays logged in and is told what went wrong

    • handleLoad

      public void handleLoad()
      Re-reads the logged-in user's save file, discarding any unsaved changes made since the last save.

      Postcondition: the library holds exactly the entries read from file, or is left untouched if the read failed

    • showDetailsFor

      public void showDetailsFor(String title)
      Looks up the entry with the given title and sends its full details to the view. Called whenever the user highlights a row in the list, which is where the polymorphic getDetails of each subclass becomes visible.

      Postcondition: the view's detail area shows the entry's details, or is cleared when nothing is selected

      Parameters:
      title - the title of the entry whose details should be shown

    • refreshView

      public void refreshView()
      Rebuilds everything the view displays from the current state of the library. Each MediaEntry is converted to a String here so that the view never touches a model object.

      Postcondition: the view's list and statistics match the library
